text:
Takeshi and I first collaborated during a campaign to boost customer retention at NijiMart. When our team noticed a 20% drop in repeat purchases during the holiday season, he proposed analyzing user behavior across our app’s onboarding flow. Over two weeks, he mapped pain points by segmenting users into cohorts based on engagement patterns. His findings revealed that 35% of users abandoned the checkout process after the second step, a detail we’d overlooked. By refining the flow and adding a progress tracker, we recovered 12% of lost conversions. It wasn’t a flashy solution, but it felt *right*—data-driven, patient, and grounded in real user needs.  

Takeshi is the kind of person who’ll spend an hour refining a chart’s axis labels to ensure clarity, then double-check with a teammate to confirm it aligns with the audience’s priorities. He’s not the loudest in meetings, but his questions often cut through noise. When our analytics team debated whether to prioritize customer acquisition or retention, he quietly built a model comparing both paths, letting the numbers speak.  

What stands out is his quiet persistence. He’ll ask, “What if we tried X?” not as a brainstorm, but as a calculated experiment. His work ethic is unshakable—once he commits to a task, he’ll iterate until it’s solid, even if it means staying late to debug a flawed assumption.  

I’d trust Takeshi to navigate ambiguity with rigor and humility. His approach isn’t just about results—it’s about asking the right questions, and then being stubborn enough to find answers.
